Case_16007/figure4.jpg.source_caption: MRI (Figure 3, with arrows added) showing leptomeningeal enhancement in the frontal lobes.

description.short_caption: MRI showing leptomeningeal enhancement in the frontal lobes.
description.detailed_description: This axial MRI image of the brain, obtained with contrast and using a FLAIR sequence, demonstrates abnormal leptomeningeal enhancement in the frontal lobes. The enhancement is highlighted by arrows, indicating areas of increased signal intensity along the meninges. The ventricles appear normal in size and shape, and there is no evidence of mass effect or midline shift.
visible_findings: leptomeningeal enhancement in the frontal lobes
no midline shift or mass effect

Case_16007/figure2.jpg.source_caption: Sagittal T1 MRI scan, VIBE sequence, with reconstruction.

description.short_caption: Sagittal T1-weighted MRI with contrast showing brain structures.
description.detailed_description: This sagittal T1-weighted MRI image with contrast demonstrates detailed visualization of the brain, including the midline structures such as the corpus callosum, brainstem, and cerebellum. The VIBE sequence provides high-resolution imaging, and the contrast enhancement highlights vascular structures and potential lesions. No obvious abnormalities are visible in this image, but further clinical correlation is necessary.
visible_findings: midline anatomy including corpus callosum and brainstem
no overt lesions or masses visible

description.short_caption: Axial T2-weighted MRI showing a lesion in the posterior fossa.
description.detailed_description: This axial T2-weighted MRI scan of the brain shows a hyperintense lesion in the posterior fossa, measuring approximately 4.2 mm in diameter. The lesion is located near the midline, adjacent to the cerebellum, and appears well-circumscribed. Surrounding structures, including the brainstem and cerebellar hemispheres, are visible. The scan is labeled with orientation markers (A, P, L, R) and includes a measurement scale.
visible_findings: hyperintense lesion in the posterior fossa
adjacent cerebellar and brainstem structures visible

Case_16007/figure3.jpg.source_caption: A post-contrast coronal T2 MRI FLAIR image.

description.short_caption: Axial post-contrast T2 FLAIR MRI of the brain.
description.detailed_description: This is an axial T2 FLAIR MRI image of the brain, taken post-contrast. The ventricles are symmetrically enlarged, and there is hyperintensity in the periventricular white matter, which may suggest inflammation, infection, or demyelination. The cortical and subcortical structures appear intact, with no evidence of mass effect or midline shift. The image is labeled as a post-contrast study, but no clear enhancement is visible in this slice.
